On Thu, Feb 9, 2012 at 9:02 AM, Kohske Takahashi
<takahash...@gmail.com> wrote:
> In general, my idea is that:
>
> 1) positional guides can be specified like
> guides(x = guide_axis(), y = guide_table(), colour = ..., fill = ...)
>
> 2) some p-guides are supported:
> - axis: similar as current axis
> - table: table
> - range: here is a good example. an absolute value is meaningless.
> only a relative distance is meaningful.

I like the idea of a guide range!

> - each guide can have their own parameters
> guide_axis(ticks = TRUE, labels = fun, grid = TRUE)
>
> - table is more complicated, and it accepts data:
> guide_table(data = df, style = ...)
> where the data is a data.frame of x (or y), text1, text2, ...
>
> the gird may be a element of axis, etc, or grid maybe a guide, so
> positional guides can be combined.
>
> guides(x = list(guide_axis(), guide_grid()))
>
> but I think probably grid should be an element of a guide.
>
> Any suggestions are welcome!!

I think the challenge of including grid in the position guides is that
it appears in a different place. I think we currently have three
types of guides:

* position (e.g. axes)
* non-position (e.g. legends)
* plot (or maybe coord) (e.g. grid)

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: removing tick from one axis
parts:
Hi,

If ggplot2 offers such new freedom for the axes, which would be
awesome, could it be possible to make it extensible by user-defined
functions too?

Some people might like to fine-tune the table guide, others would want
to include a colorbar (say of the visible spectrum -- I've used that
in the past), or a tree-graph, or and arrow, or...

Lattice allows this sort of customization (of axes, but also facet
strips, btw) by calling a custom axis function that is fed with the
breaks and returns a proper grob. Could this potentially be done in
the ggplot2 framework too?

All the best,

baptiste

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: removing tick from one axis
parts:
so you can write your own guide. We will provide a simple interface like:

input: range, breaks, minor_breaks, labels, coord(?)
output: grob (gtable), style

so you will write a function like this:

my_guide <- function(guide_info, ...) {
...
ret <- grob()
attr(ret, "style") <- "float"
ret
}

where gudie_info is a list including all information for building guide,
and style is either "float" or "b/t/l/r". If float, the position guide
will not be a part of panel gtalbe (like position = c(x, y) in
legends). if style is either b/t/l/r, then the guides are put aside
the main panel.

of course, this idea will be improved.
any comments are welcome!

thanks,

kohske

> * non-position (e.g. legends)
> * plot (or maybe coord) (e.g. grid)

Could you please explain a little bit more about the idea of plot guide?
What do you mean by that the grid appears in a different place?

Now I would think that grid can be a position guide, and guide-axis
includes the guide-grid by default.
The syntax will be like this:

guide = guide_axis(..., grid = guide_grid()) # or NULL
guide = guide_grid(...) # without axis

thanks,

kohske

>> guide = guide_grid(...) # without axis
>
> That syntax is fine - I just don't see how it would work in terms of
> how grobs are currently assembled, particularly because different
> coordinate systems need the grids drawn in different ways.

Yes, so I would think that each coord has responsibility to render the
grid lines.
At the moment, this is very similar with the positional guides.
Now guide-axis is S3 dispatch depending on the coord.

More precisely, the rendering of guide has two phase, calculation and gen-grob.
The gen-grob part can be shared among different coords, but the
calculation part should be done by each coords.
This is very similar with the grid lines.

Ok, I will try to implement this.

kohske
